_about: Battle Brothers character backgrounds, extracted from the fandom wiki dump. One row per stat table on each '(Background)' page, so variants (Southern Assassin, Barbarian/Southern Indebted, Companion 1H/2H/Ranged, Regent in Absentia, Monk turned Flagellant, Pacified Flagellant, Melee/Ranged Nomad) are their own rows. stats = the absolute [min,max] range a recruit rolls (page row 'Attribute Range'); stat_modifiers = the [min,max] the background adds to the shared base range (page row 'min./max.'); base_stats = that shared base. daily_wage = the page's Base Wage. hiring_cost is null everywhere: the wiki gives no per-background base hiring cost (Game Guide: 'from 30 for the worst ones up to around 150 for the best ones. Swordmasters are an exception with a base cost of 400!'); where the Game Guide quotes an observed hiring range it is kept as hiring_cost_game_guide_observed. Every row is cross-checked against the 'Character Backgrounds/Attribute Ranges' table and against base+modifiers; cross_check says the result. Numbers copied exactly. Extraction 2026-10-02, research only.

base_stats.quote: Character Backgrounds Attributes are not fixed but rather randomized inside ranges. Each Background shares a base range and adds modifiers on top. Apprentice is the only Background with no modifiers.
base_stats.derived_from: the Apprentice row of the Attribute Ranges table (the background with no modifiers, so its range IS the shared base range)

hiring_and_wage_rules.hiring_quote: The background defines a base hiring cost going from 30 for the worst ones up to around 150 for the best ones. Swordmasters are an exception with a base cost of 400! The cost of equipment is set at 1.25 its base value... Levels are valued thus: 500 x (level – 1) ^ 1.5. With a possible range of 1 to 5, the additional cost goes from 0 to 3,000.
hiring_and_wage_rules.wage_quote: Each background has a base daily cost which ranges from 3 to 35. This base value is multiplied by a random number between 90% and 110%. The result is then multiplied by 1.1 ^ (level – 1) for the first 11 levels (1 to 2.6 multiplier)... The cost of 11 levels is taken as a base and multiplied by 1.03 ^ (level – 11). For example, a level 11 Hedge Knight costs, with no other modifiers, 91. And on level 21, he costs 122 in daily upkeep.
